name: scheduled-chat-continuation-gate
principle: Workers do not need to decide for themselves whether they have worked long enough or whether a run should end. They report observable canonical state to the continuation/finalization scripts and follow the returned decision. Local job failure, empty paper stock, duplicate-only discovery, apparent search exhaustion, throughput counts, or transport backlog are not worker-invented run stop conditions. Special runs such as maintenance and the 08:30 update worker keep their dedicated termination rules.

decision_authority.rule: The worker's responsibility is accurate observation and execution of next_action, not subjective persistence or subjective stopping. Pass current canonical facts to the scripts and adopt their decision. Do not manufacture an error, platform limit, exhaustion claim, or other stop evidence to justify ending. CONTINUE/MUST_CONTINUE means execute the returned next action in the same invocation. A normal final response is allowed only when the finalization script returns MAY_FINALIZE with finalization_permit.issued=true.

always_on_policy.overflow_research_rule: For the :00 discovery-specialist worker, candidate_inventory > 50 with actionable research/audit means switch to overflow research mode; large inventory is a mode switch, not a run stop.
always_on_policy.rule: For a normal paper-worker run, zero actionable paper stock means discovery work exists. A single discovery round yielding zero novel candidates never proves that no independent work remains.

scheduled_handoff_policy.rule: For the hourly :00 discovery worker and hourly :30 normal paper worker, capture the actual Scheduled Chat invocation start once and define run_deadline = actual_start + run_window_seconds. Before starting another independent unit, compute seconds_to_run_deadline and pass it to continuation_gate.py. The worker does not infer from the clock that it should stop; it follows the gate result. The nominal :00/:30 boundary is compatibility fallback only when the actual-start deadline cannot be established.

discovery_specialist_progression.rule: Discovery rounds, rounds since the last novel candidate, duplicate-only rounds, candidate counts, and apparent discovery exhaustion are telemetry and search-steering inputs only. They do not authorize a normal run stop. The worker refreshes observable state, calls continuation_gate.py, and follows its required_action.

research_blocked_retry_policy.rule: Each distinct research blocked event is counted once by GitHub Actions. Attempts 1 and 2 remain blocked for a one-hour cooldown and are then returned to ready without losing block history. The third blocked event is promoted to blocked_permanent and is not automatically retried. Repeated survey-helper runs must not double-count the same blocked event.

fallback_policy.rule: GitHub is the canonical direct transport. If GitHub write is unavailable, ChatGPT Library is the only external durable outbox. On recovery, Library submits immutable envelopes to GitHub fallback-inbox. Research/audit record bundles are converted by replay_record_fallback.py into safe record-bank slots plus attempt-specific immutable descriptors; non-record envelopes use the generic allowlisted fallback transport. Historical chat-inbox bundles are read compatibility only and are never recreated.

backlog_policy.rule: Record-bank count, Library pending count, GitHub fallback-inbox count, and unsent-paper count are transport-state metrics, not research-capacity limits. Normal research/audit workers use the bank reserved by the claim result; the selector is diagnostic/maintenance/fallback-replay support.

probe_success.action: checkpoint only the affected complete logical payload through ChatGPT Library fallback when direct GitHub write still cannot preserve it, leave its GitHub job incomplete, continue independent work, and allow later unrelated GitHub writes

probe_failure.action: disable further GitHub writes for the remainder of this run; checkpoint each completed payload through ChatGPT Library; when normal GitHub ready work is exhausted, continue from fallback spillover candidates or create an offline job seed and keep researching

fallback_failure_protocol.chatgpt_library_failed: if GitHub direct write can still durably preserve required state, continue through GitHub; otherwise let continuation_gate.py classify the resulting durable-save blocker before any finalization attempt
fallback_failure_protocol.source_recovery_failed: leave the Library source pending and continue other research or GitHub-direct work; one replay failure is not itself a global stop
fallback_failure_protocol.dependency_not_materialized: leave the valid research/audit envelope in GitHub fallback-inbox until its deterministic canonical job is materialized; do not quarantine it merely for arriving before the offline seed
fallback_failure_protocol.duplicate_intake: if the same envelope id and content already exists in GitHub fallback-inbox/archive, acknowledge the Library copy without re-dispatching it
fallback_failure_protocol.id_conflict: quarantine only the conflicting envelope; do not overwrite the GitHub ledger and do not stop unrelated work

end_of_run_gate.rule: Before emitting a final response, refresh the canonical state required by the gate, pass those observations to continuation_gate.py, then pass its result plus assignment/pending-transport state to run_finalization_gate.py. Do not independently decide that enough work has been done, that discovery is exhausted, or that the run feels too long. CONTINUE or MUST_CONTINUE means execute the returned next action and reevaluate after the next durable checkpoint. STOP_RUN is only an input to finalization; a normal final response requires MAY_FINALIZE and finalization_permit.issued=true. For hourly :00 discovery and :30 normal paper workers the preferred time basis is actual invocation start + 3600 seconds, not the nominal schedule boundary. Maintenance and the 08:30 update worker retain their dedicated rules.
